reason: Holds, with one caveat on the year. The Burning Man/Scriptor Press printing the verifier used names no translator, so I checked it independently. archive.org full-text search finds the identical six lines in sunstonepiedrade0000pazo, the New Directions bilingual Sunstone/Piedra de sol (1991, associated name Eliot Weinberger, ISBN 0811211975), which ends the poem 'forever arriving:' immediately before NOTES. It also finds them in poemsofoctaviopa0000pazo (The Poems of Octavio Paz, Weinberger), with the lines broken as quoted. A different translation (Denver Quarterly 1992: 'willow of crystal ... a deep-rooted tree but dancing away') shows the Weinberger wording is distinctive, and this is it. The closing colon is closed to a full stop, which rule 6 requires. The lowercase opening 'a' is the poem's own and is correctly kept. The last six lines repeat the first six, so the fame signal is met; in the closing position they are grammatically the object of 'revived' in the preceding line, but they stand identically as the poem's opening. Caveat: I did not see the 1987 Collected Poems page. If the editor wants the edition actually seen, cite New Directions 1991. shipped.js: clean, Paz 0 of 3, not banned. The source line is 76 characters.
